The points are $P=(1,a,b)$, $Q=(a,2,b)$, $R=(a,b,3)$. They are collinear exactly when $\vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=\vec 0$.

$$\vec{PQ}=(a-1,\;2-a,\;0),\qquad \vec{PR}=(a-1,\;b-a,\;3-b)$$

The cross product is

$$\vec{PQ}\times\vec{PR}=\big((2-a)(3-b),\;-(a-1)(3-b),\;(a-1)(b-2)\big).$$

Setting each component to zero gives:

1. $(2-a)(3-b)=0$
2. $(a-1)(3-b)=0$
3. $(a-1)(b-2)=0$

**Case $a=1$:** Conditions 1 and 2 both reduce to $3-b=0$, so $b=3$. Condition 3 is then satisfied automatically. The points are $(1,1,3)$, $(1,2,3)$, $(1,3,3)$, which lie on the line $x=1,\ z=3$.

**Case $a\neq 1$:** Condition 2 forces $b=3$, and condition 3 forces $b=2$. These contradict each other, so there is no solution.

The only solution is $a=1$, $b=3$, so $a+b=4$.

ANSWER: 4
